message.content:
Here are some popular sushi restaurants in Tokyo that many locals and visitors rave about:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred; famed for precision and quality. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Intimate setting; Michelin‑starred; known for meticulous preparation. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Michelin‑starred; focuses on seasonal ingredients and subtle flavors. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Famous for fresh fish; long lines but worth the wait. |
| **Sushi Daiwa** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Similar to Sushi Dai; often less crowded but still top quality. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Classic sushi experience; well‑known for consistency and service. |
| **Sushi Sugita** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Michelin‑starred; offers a refined tasting menu. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Known for its creative takes on traditional sushi. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Shinjuku (Tokyo) | Small, intimate spot; praised for fresh fish and friendly service. |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Ginza (Tokyo) | Michelin‑starred; focuses on seasonal ingredients and minimalistic plating. |

These restaurants range from high‑end Michelin‑starred establishments to more casual yet highly regarded spots. If you’re planning a visit, it’s a good idea to make reservations in advance—especially for the Michelin‑starred places—and be prepared for potentially long waits at the Tsukiji market stalls. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
